sentences.text: This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act"), by the owner of the offending vehicle against the Judgment and Award dated 27.03.2015 partly allowing the Claim Application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Respondents, who are the dependents of deceased Shaikh Khwaja Shaikh Karamat.

2) The Respondents filed the Claim Petition No.107 of 2009 before the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Buldhana contending that, deceased Shaikh Khwaja Shaikh Karamat died due to the Motor Vehicular Accident occurred on 07.12.2008, while the deceased was travelling on the motorcycle bearing No.MH-28-N-4441 and the Appellant, who was travelling on his motorcycle bearing No.MH-28-K- 1337 and there was head-on-collision between the said vehicles.
The Respondents contended that, the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the Appellant and Kavita.
3/7 10 fa 275-15 claimed compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The Claim Petition was contested by the Appellant by filing the Written Statement.
The claim was denied.
Both the sides led their respective evidence in support of their contentions.

The learned Tribunal by the impugned Judgment and Award held 50% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and the Appellant, each and awarded the compensation of Rs.07,85,500/- with interest.
3) Heard the learned Advocate for the Appellant.
None for the Respondents.
Perused the papers on record.

4) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, though the crime was registered against the Appellant with the concerned police station, the Appellant was acquitted by the learned trial Court in Summary Criminal case No.14 of 2009.
She further submitted that, the deceased was not holding the driving license.

The claim before the learned Tribunal was of Rs.2,00,000/-,
however, the learned Tribunal has granted more compensation.

She submits that, on these grounds,
the impugned Judgment and Award be set aside and the Appeal be allowed.
Kavita.
Both the sides examined the eye witnesses to the accident.

The learned Tribunal considered the evidence of the eye witnesses and recorded the finding that, each party made the allegations to shift the negligence on each other and therefore, the learned Tribunal considered the Police papers, which were placed on record by the Respondents.

Considering the police papers and particularly, the spot panchnama, the learned Tribunal held the deceased and the Appellant each, who were driving their respective motorcycles at the time of the accident, 50% responsible for the accident.

The relevant para No.10 from the impugned Judgment is reproduced below:-
10.

The copy of F.I.R. shows that though incident took place on 7-12-2008, the pillion rider of victim- Shri. Prafulla Vasantrao Ugale vs Smt. Ruksanabi Wd/O Sk. Khwaja And ... on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26959832/

sentences.text: Prior to that, the police approached to the spot and drawn the sketch map of scene of offence.
It reveals that accident took place on straight road, which is 10 feet wide with 5 feet strip on the both sides.
There was damages to both motorcycles which was noted in the spot panchanama.
It reveals that two motorcycles, which were heading face to face, were collided.
Admittedly, motorcycles are small vehicles and therefore, they can easily cross each other.
Despite that, there was an head-on collision in two motorcycles, which itself Kavita.
5/7 10 fa 275-15 demonstrates that both motorcycle-riders are equally responsible.

Though, the claimants tried to shift negligence on the part of another motorcycle, one has to refer that after completion of investigation, the chargesheet came to be filed against opponent and as well as deceased.
Therefore, I am inclined to hold that there was a head-on collision in between two motorcycles and the accident was caused partly by deceased and partly by opponent.
It has come in the claimant's evidence that on the next date, post- mortem of dead body was conducted.
The cause of death was due to severe head injuries, which sustained by the deceased in the vehicular accident.
I have no hesitation to hold that deceased died due to the use of offending motorcycle by the opponent."
6) Perusal of the record shows that, the said finding by the learned Tribunal is based on the police papers, particularly the spot panchnama.
The sketch on the spot panchnama shows that, the spot of the accident was on the middle of the road.
The said finding and the conclusion by the learned Tribunal
cannot be faulted.

7) The copy of the Judgment by the Criminal Court, tendered across the Bar by the learned Advocate for the Appellant shows that, the Appellant was acquitted in the Criminal Case, which came to be registered in respect of the said accident.

Perusal of the said Judgment shows that, the prosecution failed to prove that, the Appellant (accused Kavita.
6/7 10 fa 275-15 therein) drove his vehicle rashly and negligently.
It is needless to stated that, the degree of proof required in the Criminal Case is that, of beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the said acquittal will not be of any assistance to the Appellant, in support of the Appeal and contention that, the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased.

8) As regard the aspect of non holding of valid driving license by the deceased is concerned, the Police papers, particularly the spot panchnama do not show that, the Appellant was on his proper side of the road.
As observed earlier, the accident took place in the middle of the road, and the Appellant is held 50% responsible for the accident.
Therefore, the said aspect that, the deceased was not holding any driving license will not be of any assistance to the Appellant.

9) As regards the contention that, the learned Tribunal awarded the claim more than what the Claimants had claimed, it is needless to state that, the Accident Claims Tribunal can award more compensation on the basis of the material available on record over and above the claim.
This Kavita.

sentences.text: 10) The learned Tribunal quantified the total amount of compensation at Rs.15,71,000/- and considered the 50% contributory negligence and passed the Award for Rs.07,85,500/- i.e. 50% of the compensation determined.

The observations and the conclusion drawn by the learned Tribunal in the impugned judgment and Award are based on the evidence available on record and no fault can be find with the same, I see no merits in the present Appeal, hence the following order.
ORDER i) The Appeal is dismissed with no orders as to costs.
ii) The R and P be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
iii) The Appeal stands disposed of.
